chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Touring with Ray Charles in 1952
summary: An agent booked Ray Charles, then living in Dallas, on a 16-day tour with Smith's band; he collapsed in San Antonio.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You've missed out the whole Ray Charles thing. How did you get together with Ray Charles?
Oh, Ray Charles was back in 1952.
Yes. What happened.
Oh, he just had a little tour around through here. The agents went out to California and booked him around through here for about 16 days, I think it was.
Was he working on his own? Or did he have a trio or what?
No. He had my band.
But what I mean is, how did you get to meet him?
Meet him? He was here! He came in here and he was staying here.
Living in Dallas.

Yeah, living here in Dallas. And the agent picked him up and booked these dates out for him, and told him to get a band together. Anyway, they all knew about me, and they just told me to get Buster and them and take a small band and go out
Buster Smith - 188
and play these dates. He can't carry more than six pieces, that's all, if he can make it. So we got together on it, these six pieces.
How did you get on with him?
All right. Until we got down in San Antonio, he got sick and had one of them jimmies. Other than that, all the rest of the dates was all right.
What was wrong with him in San Antonio?

Well, truth speaking, he had smoked one of them things, that evening just about this time -- really a little earlier, before he came to work. And the house was just full of folks. And the boys came in, and he was an hour late getting there, and I had to play the piano until he got there, and when they brought him in there, he got up there and played one number, he played "Night Train," and he jumped up and had one of them jimmies there, and they had to carry him out of there.
He went kind of crazy?
Yeah.
Good God.
Mmm-hmm.
It couldn't have been something. It must have been something stronger than that.
